Cushing’s disease is a form of hypercortisolism caused by an excessive pituitary secretion of adrenocorticotrophic hormone (ACTH). The ACTH stimulates the adrenal glands to produce cortisol. A) Taking glucocorticoids to treat asthma will cross-react with endogenous cortisol and suppress the negative feedback loop of cortisol on the hypothalamus and pituitary gland. This will lead to an increase in ACTH and therefore cortisol. This will exacerbate the symptoms of Cushing’s disease. B) Glucocorticoid receptor antagonists are drugs such as spironolactone and cyprosterone. They are used to treat the symptoms of Cushing’s disease by blocking the effects of cortisol. C) In Cushing’s disease, somatic cells are not responding to cortisol. This means that the problem is not an excess of cortisol but a desensitisation of the somatic cells to cortisol. D) Radiation therapy to treat a pituitary adenoma can damage the pituitary gland and lead to secondary hypoadrenalism. This is the opposite of Cushing’s disease.

HCN4 channels are hyperpolarised cyclic gated inwardly rectifying potassium channels. Activation of beta adrenergic receptors via noradrenaline causes an increase in cAMP which in turn activates the HCN4 channels. This causes an increase in the funny current (If) which would have a predominant effect on pacemaker cells (i.e. the SA node) and increase the rate of depolarisation. This would have a predominant effect on the chronotropy (heart rate) of the heart.  Ryanodine receptors are the receptors on the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) which are activated by an increase in intracellular Ca2+ and cause an increase in Ca2+ release from the SR. This is an important mechanism of CICR (Calcium induced calcium release).  The stimulation of these receptors would have an increase in both the Inotropy (force of contraction) and Lucitropy (rate of relaxation) of the heart.

Aldosterone is a steroid hormone that functions in the adrenal glands. It is involved in the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) and is released in response to decreased blood pressure. Aldosterone increases sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion in the kidneys, which increases blood pressure. It also stimulates the release of ADH, which increases water reabsorption by the kidneys. Therefore, aldosterone increases water retention by the kidneys.

A - Anterior cord syndrome is the correct answer. This is the most common incomplete cord injury and is often seen in older people who fall on their neck whilst forwards extending their head. The hyperextension causes narrowing of the spinal canal and therefore affects the anterior part of the spinal cord first. The anterior part contains the corticospinal and spinothalamic tracts so loss of motor function and pain/temp sensation are seen below the level of injury. However, the posterior part of the spinal cord is not affected so proprioception and 2-point discrimination are intact.B - This is a made up cord syndromeC - Posterior cord syndrome - This is rare and is caused by hyperextension of the neck which compresses the posterior part of the spinal cord. Loss of proprioception and vibratory sensation are seen below the level of injury. However, motor function and pain/temp sensation are intact.D - Brown-Sèquard syndrome - This is a delayed hemostasis which can occur after a spinal hemisection. It is characterised by sensory dissociation where the dorsal column pathway is damaged on one side of the spinal cord and the spinothalamic tract is damaged on the other. So you get loss of vibration/proprioception on the side affected and loss of pain/temp on the contralateral side.E - Paget's disease - This is a bone disorder which causes bones to be enlarged and deformed. It is not a cord syndrome.
